A program for free voice and video calls over the internet, launched in 2003. It was founded by the Swede Niklas Zennström and the Dane Janus Friis, but the software was written by Estonian engineers in Tallinn: Ahti Heinla, Priit Kasesalu and Jaan Tallinn.

The same team had built Kazaa, a file sharing program, and used its peer to peer idea: calls ran between users' computers, not through costly central exchanges. Skype made long distance and international calls nearly free and became a verb.

eBay bought it in 2005 and Microsoft in 2011. Microsoft shut it down in 2025 in favour of Teams. For Estonia, a small country that left the Soviet Union in 1991, Skype was proof of its tech boom. Its founders and early staff went on to start and fund many more companies there, and Estonia became known for digital government.
